_comment: DAT1 Task 2. Every scalar tunable below carries a validated_on_split field stating which split (if any) actually justifies its value -- see docs/SPLIT_PROTOCOL.md. Values marked UNVALIDATED are literals inherited unchanged from the pre-DAT1 pipeline and must be re-derived against VALIDATION before being cited in the paper as deliberately tuned, per SPLIT_PROTOCOL.md's per-parameter provenance table.

fedprox_mu.validated_on_split: VALIDATION-split mu-sweep (mu in {0, 0.005, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1}, task4_federated, 5 seeds x 2 modalities): network argmax=0.005 (val macro-F1 0.868 vs 0.845 at the old flat 0.02); application argmax=0 (val macro-F1 0.806 vs 0.743 at 0.02). No single mu is optimal for both modalities simultaneously, so this is now per-model_type rather than a flat scalar -- main.py's _PROX_MU_HARDCODED_DEFAULTS reads these two values directly (not via get_value(_HP_CONFIG, 'fedprox_mu')); --prox-mu on the CLI still overrides both, e.g. for the mu-sweep experiment itself.

dp_max_grad_norm.validated_on_split: UNVALIDATED -- inherited from pre-DAT1 pipeline; no VALIDATION-split clipping-norm sweep has been run yet.

adaptive_krum_k.validated_on_split: UNVALIDATED -- inherited from pre-DAT1 pipeline; pending a VALIDATION-split MAD-k sweep (see mad_k_sweep_default below). Also used as the default for --krum-k / HEAD_NORM_GUARD_K when not overridden on the CLI.

adaptive_krum_hybrid_assumed_f.validated_on_split: UNVALIDATED as a tuned value -- this is the operator's ASSUMED attacker-count cap fed into min(assumed_f, NUM_BYZANTINE) for the HE+Krum hybrid (Experiment 2), not a value fit to any split. Experiment 2's own assumed-f-mismatch ablation is the closest thing to a validation of this parameter's sensitivity to date; see byzantine_f_sweep_default below for the sweep range.

class_weight_multipliers_application.validated_on_split: REMOVED -- no manual per-class multipliers are applied (all 1.0 = neutral). The pre-DAT1 values (Uploading 1.3, XSS 1.5, Fingerprinting 1.3) were chosen against a test-adjacent metric (each client's own local held-out split, before a global TEST holdout existed) and were not re-derived on the global VALIDATION split, so they were dropped rather than carried forward as unjustified tuning. The application criterion now uses only the inverse-sqrt class weights (clamped at a 5.0 max ratio) with FocalLoss gamma=2.0; none of these were tuned against TEST. The VALIDATION mu-sweep recorded under fedprox_mu was run with all three at 1.0 (VM config), so this file now matches the configuration that produced it. The keys are retained at 1.0 so config validation and task.py keep a single code path. See task.py:build_criterion_application() docstring, history item 5.

trimmed_mean_beta.validated_on_split: UNVALIDATED -- new BAS1 (Issue 3) baseline-comparison knob, not yet swept against any split.
